page.description: OpenWrt 25.12.6 for x86/64: compare image types, download firmware images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Linux distribution targeting embedded devices — mainly routers — providing a fully writable filesystem with package management.
pros: GPG-signed checksums establish a chain of trust from publisher to firmware image.
x86 combined images boot both UEFI and legacy BIOS from one file.
ext4 rootfs variant gives more usable space than the default squashfs.
Single image serves as both the initial install and the sysupgrade firmware.
cons: Distributed per-device as router firmware; the x86 target is secondary and not the primary use case.
The squashfs image has less than 100 MB free space for additional packages.
A data-loss bug affects systems with multiple block devices (Issue#20426).
No screenshot with a reusable licence was available, so this page is logo-only.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was available for OpenWrt; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the raw disk image (combined-efi.img.gz or combined.img.gz) directly to the target drive with dd; the publisher warns 'Writing the raw image file will DELETE content on the drive.' For x86, use the same image for initial install and sysupgrade. The combined-efi variant boots UEFI, the plain variant boots BIOS. A -combined image overwrites the partition table and deletes any extra partitions.

editions.name: x86/64 SquashFS Combined EFI
editions.description: SquashFS rootfs with combined partition layout booting UEFI (and BIOS via hybrid MBR); the recommended x86/64 image for most users.
editions.usbNote: 12 MB gzipped raw disk image. Write it with dd to the target drive; writing erases the drive. This is a combined image — writing it overrides the partition table.

editions.name: x86/64 ext4 Combined EFI
editions.description: ext4 rootfs with combined partition layout booting UEFI (and BIOS); provides more usable space than squashfs but loses failsafe mode.
editions.usbNote: 13 MB gzipped raw disk image. Write it with dd to the target drive; writing erases the drive. This is a combined image — writing it overrides the partition table.
